title: API gateway authentication: APIM vs API Gateway vs Istio
summary: Every gateway handles identity twice: it checks the caller's token, then calls the backend as its own identity. The platforms differ in where the check is configured and what the backend learns about the caller.

dimensions.label: Caller's token checked by
values: validate-azure-ad-token or validate-jwt policy
JWT authorizer (HTTP API); Cognito or Lambda authorizer (REST API)
securityDefinitions in the OpenAPI spec
RequestAuthentication + AuthorizationPolicy

dimensions.label: Service callers without a user
values: Entra token for a managed identity or app
IAM authorization with SigV4
Google-signed token from a service account
mTLS SPIFFE identity, matched by principals

dimensions.label: Gateway → backend as
values: APIM's managed identity
Lambda resource policy for apigateway.amazonaws.com
The API config's backend service account
The gateway's Kubernetes service account, over mTLS

dimensions.label: Backend learns the caller from
values: Whatever the policies forward: the token, claims in headers, or nothing
Checked claims in the request context
The original token in X-Forwarded-Authorization
Nothing by default; forwardOriginalToken or outputPayloadToHeader

dimensions.label: API keys
values: Subscription keys: quotas and analytics
Usage-plan keys: throttling and quotas
API keys: identify the project
None built in

dimensions.label: Keeping callers from skipping it
values: Private endpoint or access restrictions, plus an app role for APIM
SourceArn on the resource policy; private integration for VPC backends
run.invoker for the gateway's service account only
PeerAuthentication STRICT + allow only the gateway principal

notes: In all four, the gateway proves who it is to the backend with its own identity. Forwarding the caller's token is optional, and only safe when the backend checks the token's audience as well.
None of the platforms treat API keys as authentication. Use them for metering, next to a real token.
A gateway only protects what can't be reached without it. Lock each backend to the gateway's identity or network.
